name: KSyntaxHighlighting
description: KDE Frameworks' C++/Qt engine with a large XML syntax catalog; used by Kate and Qt Creator

host-language.comment: C++ library built on Qt (Qt Core/Gui; no Qt Widgets/QML requirement). Also exposes a QML API (src/quick), which is consumed from Qt apps rather than a separate host language.

form-factor.comment: KF6::SyntaxHighlighting library plus the bundled `ksyntaxhighlighter` CLI (HTML/ANSI output, syntax tracing for grammar authors).

license.comment: Engine code is MIT (SPDX headers; README says contributions are MIT). Originally announced as LGPLv2+ in 2016 and later relicensed. Individual syntax definition XML files carry their own licences (e.g. html.xml LGPL, rust.xml MIT, Qt Creator lists java.xml as LGPL-2.1); the LICENSES folder also holds BSD-2/3, CC0, GPL-2.0-only, GPL-3.0-or-later, LGPL-2.0/2.1-or-later texts.

repository.comment: Canonical repo on KDE's GitLab (invent.kde.org); read-only mirror at github.com/KDE/syntax-highlighting.

package.comment: No language-registry package; distributed as KDE Frameworks source tarballs (syntax-highlighting-6.32.0.tar.xz) and via distro packages (e.g. kf6-syntax-highlighting).

documentation.comment: QDoc-generated API reference on api.kde.org plus the repo README; syntax/theme catalogs on kate-editor.org.

first-release.comment: First shipped as a new framework in KDE Frameworks 5.28.0 on 2016-11-15. The underlying Kate highlighting engine and XML format are much older (inside KTextEditor).

latest-version.comment: KDE Frameworks 6.32.0, announced 2026-11-13; latest tag as of 2026-11-18. Versioned in lockstep with monthly KDE Frameworks releases.

engine-model.comment: Interprets Kate XML syntax definitions (context stack with DetectChar/keyword/RegExpr rules). The reference kde-syntax engine.

regex-engine.comment: RegExpr rules use Qt's QRegularExpression, which is backed by PCRE2. Many rules are non-regex (DetectChar, StringDetect, keyword lists, Int/Float), so regex is only part of the matching.

embedded-languages.comment: html.xml includes `##CSS` for style elements and `Normal##JavaScript` for script elements (plus JSX) through cross-definition IncludeRules, so HTML+JS+CSS works out of the box.

language-auto-detection.comment: Definitions are looked up only by name, file name/extension, or MIME type; there is no content-based guessing API.

filename-extension-mapping.comment: Repository::definitionForFileName / definitionsForFileName (extensions + mimetype, priority-ranked) and definitionForMimeType.

resumable-line-state.comment: highlightLine(text, State) returns the next opaque State, which the docs say can be stored for partial re-highlighting while editing.

incremental-reparsing.comment: No parse tree to reuse. Edits are handled by re-highlighting from the stored per-line State, which counts as Resumable Line State only.

semantic-distinctions.comment: Lexical context-stack engine with no syntax tree or locals tracking. The README explicitly leaves anything beyond highlighting and folding ranges to KTextEditor.

bundled-languages.comment: kate-editor.org/syntax (checked 2026-11-18) says KSyntaxHighlighting supports 466 languages. This counts syntax definitions, some of which are dialects or helper/sub-languages. The data/syntax directory has 417 entries; some definitions are generated at build time.

grammar-format.comment: Kate XML syntax definitions in data/syntax, validated against an XSD schema (validatehl.sh). Compiled into the library as Qt resources (CBOR-indexed) at build time.

grammar-ecosystem-compatibility.comment: Consumes only Kate/KDE XML definitions; the reference implementation of that ecosystem (also reused by skylighting and Qt Creator). Cannot load TextMate, Sublime, or tree-sitter grammars.

runtime-grammar-loading.comment: Repository::addCustomSearchPath (disk or Qt resource paths) and per-user org.kde.syntax-highlighting/syntax directories. File-system definitions override built-in ones; DefinitionDownloader can fetch updates.

lazy-grammar-loading.comment: The Repository reads only metadata for every definition ("moderately expensive" at construction). Contexts and rules are parsed on first use via DefinitionData::load(), with a keywords-only partial load mode. All definitions still ship compiled into the library.

grammar-accuracy.comment: Spot check 2026-11-18: python.xml (v33) covers match/case and f-strings; rust.xml covers async/union. typescript.xml (v18) has no `satisfies` (TS 4.9), `override`, or `asserts` keywords. Grammars are hand-maintained by KDE rather than tracking an upstream grammar. Well regression-tested, with active per-release fixes (e.g. C++ #embed in 6.32). Rated 3 for known gaps on modern syntax.

bundled-themes.comment: 30 .theme files in data/themes on master (checked 2026-11-18, ~6.32), e.g. Breeze, Atom One, Catppuccin, Dracula, GitHub, Gruvbox, Monokai, Nord, Solarized, Tokyo Night, plus a Printing theme.

theme-format.comment: JSON .theme files mapping the 31 default text styles and editor colours; per-definition overrides possible.

token-classification.comment: Each grammar's itemData maps to one of 31 Theme::TextStyle default styles (Keyword, Function, ControlFlow, String, Comment, …). Format::name() also exposes the grammar-specific itemData name.

css-class-output.comment: The built-in HtmlHighlighter writes `<span style="color:…;background-color:…">` inline styles only; there is no class-based mode.

multi-theme-output.comment: HTML output resolves one theme to inline colours; there is no single-render light/dark mechanism.

public-token-api.comment: Documented AbstractHighlighter: subclass it, call highlightLine(), and receive applyFormat(offset, length, Format) callbacks (plus applyFolding for folding regions). This is a callback stream, not a returned collection.

ir-kinds.comment: Per-line (offset, length, Format) spans delivered via callback. A Format carries a name and TextStyle (token class) and resolves colours/bold/italic against a Theme (styled span). Folding regions are delivered as separate events. No tree or JSON form.

serializable-ir.comment: Format and State are in-memory C++ objects (State is opaque); there is no documented serialization.

theme-resolved-tokens.comment: Format::textColor(theme), isBold(theme), etc. resolve the style for the current Theme. The SyntaxHighlighter class applies them directly to a QTextDocument.

source-offsets-in-ir.comment: applyFormat/applyFolding receive offset and length within the current line (line index is tracked by the caller).

custom-formatter-api.comment: The docs say to subclass AbstractHighlighter and reimplement applyFormat() to produce your own output. The bundled HTML/ANSI highlighters are built this way.

line-transforms-decorations.comment: No built-in line/range annotation mechanism; decorations are left to the host editor (e.g. KTextEditor).

output-formats.comment: ksyntaxhighlighter `-f html|ansi|ansi256`: inline-styled HTML, 24-bit ANSI, and xterm-256 ANSI (no 16-colour mode). HtmlHighlighter/AnsiHighlighter are exported for the bundled CLI but not listed in the public class docs. The library also offers a QSyntaxHighlighter subclass for Qt rich-text documents (no matching tag).

line-numbers.comment: Neither the CLI options nor the HTML/ANSI highlighters offer line-number output.

streaming-output.comment: Input is read and highlighted line by line. The documented `-U/--unbuffered` option (ansi/ansi256) flushes output after each line. The library's highlightLine API is inherently line-incremental.

terminal-ready.comment: The bundled CLI emits truecolor or 256-colour ANSI directly.

native-dependencies.comment: Native C++ library that requires Qt 6 and is built with CMake/ECM. Regex is provided by Qt (PCRE2).

runs-in-browser.comment: No official browser build. Qt for WebAssembly could in principle host it, but nothing is documented.

wasm-build.comment: No official or documented wasm32 target.

synchronous-api.comment: highlightLine() is a plain synchronous call; only the Repository construction does up-front (synchronous) metadata loading.

bindings-ports.comment: No official bindings beyond C++ and QML. The Kate XML format is reimplemented independently by skylighting (Haskell, separate candidate), and Qt Creator vendors the C++ library.

core-package-size.comment: Native Qt library (bundles compiled-in syntax/theme resources); not comparable with JS bundle or registry package sizes.

throughput-tier.comment: No independent or reproducible cross-engine benchmark found; release notes mention ongoing performance work (shared regex cache, skip offsets) but no comparative numbers.

initialization-cost.comment: Not measured. The Repository constructor loads metadata for all definitions (documented as moderately expensive) and per-definition rules load lazily, but no timing is published.

github-stars.comment: Stars on the read-only GitHub mirror KDE/syntax-highlighting as of 2026-11-18. Development happens on invent.kde.org, so stars understate adoption.

monthly-downloads.comment: No language package registry; shipped as KDE Frameworks tarballs and distro packages, so no comparable download metric.

maintenance-status.comment: Monthly KDE Frameworks releases with engine and syntax changes; mirror last pushed 2026-11-18.

documentation-quality.comment: Rated 3: solid README, a QDoc API reference covering all public classes, and a syntax catalog on kate-editor.org. There are no usage guides or examples beyond the CMake snippet, and no migration notes.

notable-users.value: Kate / KWrite / KDevelop (via KTextEditor), Qt Creator (generic highlighter)
notable-users.comment: KTextEditor switched to KSyntaxHighlighting in KF 5.29. Qt Creator vendors it in src/libs/3rdparty/syntax-highlighting for its generic highlighter. Pandoc reuses the XML definitions through skylighting, not this library.

bus-factor.comment: Part of KDE Frameworks, maintained by KDE contributors with monthly release engineering.
